Satvika Veeravalli on ‘Aakasamlo Oka Tara’: Quitting a corporate career for films was serendipity
 The actor, who makes her debut as an aspiring astronaut in director Pavan Sadineni’s Telugu film co-starring Dulquer Salmaan, discusses her Telugu roots, and learning to act on set
 Published - November 18, 2026 07:00 am IST 
 Sangeetha Devi Dundoo READ LATER 
 SEE ALL 
 Remove 
 Satvika Veeravalli and Dulquer Salmaan in ‘Aakasamlo Oka Tara’
 | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement
 In the Telugu film Aakasamlo Oka Tara , releasing on November 20, newcomer Satvika Veeravalli plays Kalpana, a young woman from a small town in Andhra Pradesh, aspiring to be an astronaut. “A part of the story takes place in Andhra Pradesh, before moving to Hyderabad and later, Chicago. In a way, it felt like the reverse of my family’s journey,” Satvika says with a laugh.
 Born and raised in Chicago, USA, Satvika reveals that her father, who hails from Veeravalli in Krishna district, Andhra Pradesh, later moved to Hyderabad for studies. While promoting the film, Satvika has been making sincere efforts to speak in Telugu and says it is a learning process. “Ethnically, I am part Telugu and part Tamil, and culturally I lean towards Tamil. Telugu is a beautiful language, and my desire to learn it has grown over the last two years.”
 Aaksasmlo Oka Tara (AOT), directed by Pavan Sadineni , also stars Dulquer Salmaan, Shruti Haasan and Ruhani Sharma. Satvika was offered the film in December 2024, following which she resigned from her job at an IT firm. The film’s team revealed her identity through a character poster only in January 2026. “I did not sign any other film. In between schedules, while my co-stars worked on other films, I had nothing to do. Those were tough days. I kept my focus on the big picture, waiting for the film to be completed,” says Satvika. 
 Reflecting on her journey into cinema, she says, “I enjoyed watching films, but never aspired to be in one. It was serendipitous.”
 An Instagram reel she had posted caught the attention of one of the producers of the Tamil film Kaantha, and she was asked to audition for the female lead role. “Though I did not land that role, the producer showed my audition video to director Pavan Sadineni when he was on the lookout for a fresh face for AOT , and I auditioned again.”
 Shivathmika Rajashekar on ‘ENE Repeat’: I never imagined myself in such a massive mainstream film Before holding forth on what made her quit a stable corporate job for a career in the movies, she takes a slight detour. Growing up in the US, she was initiated into Carnatic music and Bharatanatyam. “My mother taught Bharatanatyam in Chicago. I instinctively leaned towards dance and enjoyed it more than music.”
 While pursuing a Master’s in engineering management at Vanderbilt University in Nashville, she felt a void in the absence of creative pursuits that had given her immense joy in her earlier years, although she enjoyed the course. “I was considering pursuing a PhD or taking up an MBA programme. When I moved to New York, I observed how a lot of people were pursuing a corporate career while also doing something in the arts. My void grew bigger. So, when this film offer came my way, I took it up.”
 Satvika Veeravalli and Dulquer Salmaan in the film
 | Photo Credit: 
 Special Arrangement
 Satvika learnt the basics of dialogue delivery during a brief workshop prior to filming and picked up the nuances of acting on set. “The proclivity I had for observing people from a young age helped. DQ ( Dulquer Salmaan ) Sir also gave me valuable insights. We spoke about observing people and their mannerisms to understand their psyche. In the US, or largely in the Western culture, inflections of the voice and pacing are used to convey emotions. In the Eastern world, people use their hands a lot more to express their emotions. It was tough for me to incorporate that while playing the character.”
 Satvika shares how Dulquer also pointed out that people in a village may not put their hands into their pockets for style or ego. “Understanding the socioeconomic background of a character is important.”
 During schedule breaks, there were times she missed the corporate routine. “Even if it was monotonous, there was a purpose to each day. I also missed my parents, friends and having a social life.”
 She soon channelised her energy into watching movies. She recalls watching the re-release of Khaleja at a single-screen theatre in Hyderabad. “I hadn’t watched several films closely and wanted to change that. I began watching new releases in theatres. I also caught up on Telugu, Tamil, Hindi and Malayalam films I had missed.”
 Jr NTR announces his next with Anil Ravipudi Asked whether she has a long-term plan for her acting career or prefers taking one step at a time, Satvika says she goes by her instincts. “Again, the advice from DQ Sir holds me in good stead. He said that whatever film I choose, I should have conviction in it despite the vitriol and box office results. My gut feeling governs my decisions.” 
 In film circles, there has been buzz about her being considered for a film with director Sukumar and Ram Charan. Satvika says with a laugh, “I have been in talks with a few production houses, but I cannot disclose details. Some are just rumours, while there are other confirmed projects.”
